title: Cross-stitch birth announcement sampler
subtitle: A personalised birth record with name, date and weight on 14-count Aida
excerpt: A traditional birth record sampler with space for name, birth date, weight, and length, surrounded by a border of small stars and hearts. The design is approximately 110 by 130 stitches on 14-count white Aida and finishes at about 20 by 23 cm. The alphabet and numeral chart is included so the stitcher can fill in the details specific to each child.
sourceNotes: Original design. Birth record samplers are a well-established category in British cross-stitch tradition; the format has appeared in UK needlework publications since the 19th century.

content.text: A birth sampler is one of the few cross-stitch pieces that cannot be worked ahead of time: the name and date are filled in from the birth. The layout gives fixed positions for each data line; the stitcher centres each personalised entry using the included alphabet chart.

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 3689 (light mauve), 3688 (medium mauve), 3721 (dark shell pink) — border and hearts; 336 (navy) — text; 368 (light pistachio), 320 (medium pistachio) — leaf border details; 744 (pale yellow) — stars

content.text: Top section: decorative heading motif (crib or stork, stitched from chart)
First text row: child's name (centred using the alphabet chart)
Second text row: date of birth in dd Month yyyy format
Third text row: weight and length
Border: small stars and heart motifs repeating on all four sides
Stitch the fixed elements before the personalisation.
Work the border, the heading motif, and any decorative divider lines first. These do not change between recipients.
Plan the name row carefully before stitching.

Count the stitch width of the full name using the alphabet chart. Mark the centre of the name row on the fabric and count left to the first letter starting point before stitching. A long name may need a slightly finer alphabet version from the chart.
Stitch the date row in the same way.
Centre the date string the same as the name. Use the numeral section of the alphabet chart for the day number and year.
Add the weight and length row last.
Use kg and cm as the units (convert from lbs and inches if needed). Centre as with the other text rows.

Birth samplers are usually framed rather than displayed in a hoop. A 25 × 30 cm mount with a white or pale pink card surround, in a plain white or light wood frame, is the most straightforward presentation.
